# ExtFn

> Browser extension configuration, runtime, build, scan, and packaging for Chromium and Firefox.

## Documentation

- [CLI workflow](https://extfn.com/docs/cli) — Develop, build, scan, and package extension targets.
- [Configuration](https://extfn.com/docs/configuration) — Choose targets, background handlers, page surfaces, and content mounts.
- [Content and background handlers](https://extfn.com/docs/content-and-background) — Register multiple content modules and discover background handlers.
- [Getting started](https://extfn.com/docs/getting-started) — Define an extension and run the canonical ExtFn workflow.
- [ExtFn](https://extfn.com/docs) — Code-first browser extension development for Chromium and Firefox.
- [Integrations and Svelte](https://extfn.com/docs/integrations) — Keep domain contracts and host adapters with their owners.
- [Operations and limits](https://extfn.com/docs/operations-and-limits) — Supported browser targets, manual steps, and validation boundaries.
- [CLI reference](https://extfn.com/docs/reference/cli) — Develop, build, scan, and package extension targets.
- [Consumer host abstraction](https://extfn.com/docs/reference/consumer-host-abstraction) — Move SvelteKit runtime dependencies behind consumer-owned adapters.
- [Reference](https://extfn.com/docs/reference) — Source-aligned ExtFn guides and examples.
- [Content and background handlers](https://extfn.com/docs/reference/multi-content-and-background-handlers) — Multiple content modules, message handlers, ports, and Svelte mounts.
- [Scanner and report](https://extfn.com/docs/reference/scan) — Strict scan rules, findings, formats, and packaging behavior.
- [Runtime and browser access](https://extfn.com/docs/runtime) — Use the Promise-first browser facade, messaging, events, and capabilities.
- [Scan and package](https://extfn.com/docs/scan-and-package) — Interpret strict findings and produce extension archives.
